- Blank lines inside a passage are kept. Leading and trailing ones are not.

## Beyond the Walls

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01_beyond_the_walls.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01_beyond_the_walls.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** elder · **Turn-in:** scout

### title

Beyond the Walls

### summary

The bells beneath the altar rang again and the seal is thinning. The Elder has sent the Order's newest Oathkeeper to the scout camped past the north gate, who keeps the road and the rite that puts the dead king back to sleep.

### offer_line

Elder: The bells rang beneath the altar last night, and the watch falls to you. Our scout is camped past the north gate. He keeps that road, and he keeps the rite with it. Find him, hear what he has seen, and do as he tells you. Will you go?

### accept_option

I'll find him.

### refuse_option

Not today.

### accepted_line

Elder: Follow the road north and keep to it. Come back and tell me what he says.

### refused_line

Elder: Then rest. The seal will hold a few days yet, and so will I.

### reoffer_line

Elder: The scout is still out there past the gate, and the bells have not stopped. Have you changed your mind?

### progress_line

Elder: Have you found the scout yet?

### continue_option

Still looking.

### abandon_option

I can't go out there.

### abandoned_line

Elder: I understand. It is no small thing to ask of anyone, whatever the tradition says. Come back if your heart changes.

### complete_line

Scout: The Elder sent you up? Then it is your turn at the altar. Good. I have walked that road with more champions than I care to count, and I tell every one of them the same thing: the rite comes first, the knight comes second, and the king comes last. We start at the beginning. Take these.

### done_line

Elder: You found the scout. Good. Do as he says, and in the order he says it. The road has only ever killed the ones who skipped ahead.

---

## A Second Oath

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01a_a_second_oath.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01a_a_second_oath.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01_beyond_the_walls`

### title

A Second Oath

### summary

The Scout will not let anyone carry the rite up the ruined road on a single partner. Loambucks graze the meadow west of his camp, and a Loambuck can mend its partners in the middle of a fight.

### offer_line

Scout: First thing, and do not argue it. Nobody carries the rite up that road alone. An Emberling alone burns hot and burns out, and everything between here and the altar is older than it is. You want someone at its back. Loambucks graze the meadow west of this camp. They are slow, but they mend. Bind one.

### accept_option

I'll bind a Loambuck.

### refuse_option

Not yet.

### accepted_line

Scout: Knock it about a little first. A tired Loambuck takes the scroll far more readily than a fresh one. Don't overdo it, mind.

### refused_line

Scout: Suit yourself. The meadow isn't going anywhere, and neither is the altar.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Still going it alone? Loambucks, west of here. Bind one.

### progress_line

Scout: Any luck in the meadow? West of the camp, in the tall grass.

### continue_option

Still looking.

### abandon_option

I'd rather not.

### abandoned_line

Scout: Your choice. Don't say I didn't warn you.

### complete_line

Scout: That's a fine one. Look at it, already sniffing your Emberling for scrapes. Keep it close. Fire will not serve you up there; half of what the dead king left behind is fire already. Things that grow are the one thing he never had. I'll show you why.

### done_line

Scout: A Loambuck at your back is worth three scrolls in your pack.

---

## Room for More

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01b_room_for_more.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01b_room_for_more.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01a_a_second_oath`

### title

Room for More

### summary

Three Oathbound walk with you and no more, but nothing you bind is ever turned away: whatever will not fit walks down to the Hearthside and waits in the paddock until you send for it. Sending one away and calling it back is done from the party page.

### offer_line

Scout: Before you get attached to those two, learn the rule. Three walk with you. Only three, ever; more than that and you are managing a crowd instead of fighting. But nothing you bind is wasted: whatever will not fit goes down to the paddock at the Hearthside, where it is fed and kept and healed, and it waits there until you send for it. Open your party page and try it, here, where nothing is chasing you.

### accept_option

Show me the paddock.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

Scout: Tab opens it, or the party button up top. Pick one of yours and send it to keeping, then call it straight back out. That is the whole system. Do it once and you will never be afraid to use a scroll again.

### refused_line

Scout: Then you will stand in a meadow full of Oathbound one day with three slots and no idea what to do about it.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Ready to learn where the spare ones go?

### progress_line

Scout: Party page. Tab. Send one to keeping, and call it back when you see how it works.

### continue_option

I'll try it now.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

Scout: When you are ready.

### complete_line

Scout: That is it. Fed, healed and waiting, and you can trade any of them in or out whenever you like. Now use your scrolls freely: a full party is no reason to walk past something worth having. Right, back to the fire. There is a thing your Loambuck can do that nobody has shown you.

### done_line

Scout: Three walk, the rest are kept. Bind everything.

---

## Field Mending

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01c_field_mending.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01c_field_mending.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01b_room_for_more`

### title

Field Mending

### summary

The Scout wants to show how a mender fights before the altar road teaches it the hard way: a healer can patch up a partner on the bench, not only itself.

### offer_line

Scout: Second thing. That road is long and nothing on it waits for you to be ready. Let me show you how a mender fights, before you learn it the hard way. Stay by the fire a moment.

### accept_option

Show me.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

Scout: Here's the thing most folk get wrong. A healer doesn't only mend itself. It can mend whoever it's sworn to, even one sitting out the fight.

### refused_line

Scout: Later, then. Don't leave it too long; the bells won't wait on you.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Ready for that lesson now?

### progress_line

Scout: Want to go again? Swap, mend, swap back.

### continue_option

Let's go again.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

Scout: Come find me when you want to try again.

### complete_line

Scout: See? Your Emberling would have burned out on its own. Swap, mend, swap back. Remember that and the road won't kill you. Sit down again, though. Mending is what you do after a blow lands, and I would rather teach you the blow.

### done_line

Scout: Swap, mend, swap back.

---

## Who Walks in Front

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01d_who_walks_in_front.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01d_who_walks_in_front.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01c_field_mending`

### title

Who Walks in Front

### summary

Whichever Oathbound walks at your shoulder is the one that opens every fight, throws every blow you swing in the field and takes every blow swung at you. Which one that is can be changed at any time from the party page.

### offer_line

Scout: One more thing off the page, and it matters more than it sounds. The one walking at your shoulder is not decoration. It opens every fight, it throws whatever you swing out here, and it wears whatever gets swung at you. So it should never be whichever one happened to be first. Going somewhere cold and wet? Put the one that likes cold and wet in front. Open the page and change it.

### accept_option

Let me see.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

Scout: Tab, then the front button under whichever one you want leading. Try it. Look at the little one following you afterwards; that is who is in front now.

### refused_line

Scout: Then whoever is first stays first, and one day that will be the wrong one.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Ready to choose who walks in front?

### progress_line

Scout: Party page, Tab. Put somebody else in front.

### continue_option

I'll change it.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

Scout: Your shoulder, your choice.

### complete_line

Scout: There. Do that before every fight you can see coming, and half the fights you cannot. Right: that is everything the page can teach you. The rest is the field, and the field starts with the key you have not used yet.

### done_line

Scout: Whoever is in front takes the first blow. Choose on purpose.

---

## Strike First

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01e_strike_first.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01e_strike_first.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01d_who_walks_in_front`

### title

Strike First

### summary

The Scout has watched you stand and wait for things to come at you. Out on the road the first blow is usually the one that decides the fight, and it is thrown with F, in the open, before a battle ever opens.

### offer_line

Scout: Third thing, and it is the one that keeps you alive. You have been standing about waiting for these things to come to you. Don't. Out here you hit first. Press F and whichever Oathbound walks at your shoulder throws its best blow the way you're facing. Land it before the fight opens and you start that fight a turn up. Let me find you something to practise on.

### accept_option

Show me.

### refuse_option

Later.

### accepted_line

Scout: There's one in the grass down the slope. Walk up on it and hit F. Close enough to touch, mind; your partner has arms, not a bow.

### refused_line

Scout: Suit yourself. Stand and wait, then, and see how that goes for you.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Ready to learn to swing first?

### progress_line

Scout: Get close and press F. That's all there is to it.

### continue_option

I'll go and hit it.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

Scout: Fine. It'll be in the grass when you change your mind.

### complete_line

Scout: That's it. See how it came into the fight already bleeding? Do that every time. Now sit back down, because the next lesson is the same one from the wrong end.

### done_line

Scout: F, and close. Never wait to be swung at.

---

## Caught in the Open

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01f_caught_in_the_open.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01f_caught_in_the_open.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01e_strike_first`

### title

Caught in the Open

### summary

Everything the Scout taught about swinging first works just as well on you. A hostile creature that reaches you lands a real blow and takes the first turn of the fight, and it is better to learn that at his fire than on the ruined road.

### offer_line

Scout: Now the same lesson from the other end, and you will not enjoy it. Some things out here hunt. They see you, they come, they wind up, and if you are still standing there when they finish winding up, they open the fight with a free blow and the first turn besides. I would rather you felt that once, here, where I can pick you up afterwards.

### accept_option

Let it come.

### refuse_option

I'd rather not.

### accepted_line

Scout: Stand still. Watch the way it gathers itself before it strikes: that pause is the whole of your warning, and it is long enough to swing or to step back. This once, don't. Take it.

### refused_line

Scout: No, nobody wants to. It happens anyway.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Ready to be knocked about for your own good?

### progress_line

Scout: It's coming. Stand and take it, then finish the fight.

### continue_option

Send it at me.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

Scout: Another time, then. It is a cheap lesson here and a dear one up the road.

### complete_line

Scout: Feel that? It hit before you had a screen to look at, and it moved first on top of it. That is exactly what you did to the last one. Stay there, we are not done with that key yet. There is one more thing a good swing does, and it is my favourite thing about it.

### done_line

Scout: Watch for the wind-up. It is the only warning you get.

---

## No Battle At All

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01g_no_battle_at_all.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01g_no_battle_at_all.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01f_caught_in_the_open`

### title

No Battle At All

### summary

A blow big enough to finish a creature outright never opens a battle screen: it falls in the grass where it stands, and it still pays what it would have paid. The Scout would rather the player learned that now than found it out by accident halfway up the road.

### offer_line

Scout: One more on that key, and this is the part nobody believes until they see it. If your swing is bigger than what is left of the thing you swing at, there is no battle. None. It goes down in the grass, you collect what it was carrying, and you keep walking. That is how a long road gets walked: you do not fight everything on it, you step over most of it.

### accept_option

Show me that.

### refuse_option

Another time.

### accepted_line

Scout: I'll find you something small. Don't feel clever about it; it is half dead already, and that is the whole point. Big swing, little thing, no fight.

### refused_line

Scout: Then you will fight every last thing between here and the altar, and you will be very tired by the end of it.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Want to see what a big swing does to a little thing?

### progress_line

Scout: It's still down there. Get close and hit it with F; it will not survive it.

### continue_option

I'll put it down.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

Scout: As you like. The grass is full of them.

### complete_line

Scout: No screen, no turns, no scrolls, and your purse is heavier anyway. Learn to read what is worth a fight and what is worth a swing and this road gets a good deal shorter. Right. That is everything I know about hitting things. Two errands before you go, and neither of them is a fight.

### done_line

Scout: If it is nearly dead, do not fight it. Swing at it.

---

## A Bed at the Hearthside

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01h_a_bed_at_the_hearthside.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01h_a_bed_at_the_hearthside.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout · **Turn-in:** innkeeper

**Follows:** `quest_main_01g_no_battle_at_all`

### title

A Bed at the Hearthside

### summary

The Scout will not send anyone up the ruined road on a tired party. A night at the Hearthside Inn, down through the gate, mends every Oathbound to full and costs nothing, and the bed you slept in is where you wake if the road puts you down.

### offer_line

Scout: Look at the pair of them. Scorched, footsore and half asleep on their feet. Go back down through the gate and take a bed at the Hearthside; the Innkeeper keeps one for the Order's own and asks nothing for it. A night there mends your Oathbound to the last scratch, and better than that, it is somewhere to wake up. Go down, sleep, and tell her I sent you.

### accept_option

A bed sounds good.

### refuse_option

We're fine.

### accepted_line

Scout: Straight back down the road and into the town. The Innkeeper is up by the pond, east side. Talk to her and she'll put you to bed.

### refused_line

Scout: You are not fine. You will be less fine tomorrow.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Changed your mind about that bed?

### progress_line

Scout: The Hearthside. Down through the gate, east side of the town, by the pond.

### continue_option

I'm going.

### abandon_option

I'd rather push on.

### abandoned_line

Scout: Stubborn. The offer stands.

### complete_line

Innkeeper: There. Fed, watered and mended, and not a coin between us. Any night you want it, the bed is here, and if something out there puts your Oathbound down, this is where you will wake up, so remember the way. Take this salve as well. And stay where you are a moment, I am not finished with you.

### done_line

Innkeeper: Bed's always made. Sleep costs you nothing but the night.

---

## A Stocked Satchel

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01i_a_stocked_satchel.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01i_a_stocked_satchel.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** innkeeper · **Turn-in:** apothecary

**Follows:** `quest_main_01h_a_bed_at_the_hearthside`

### title

A Stocked Satchel

### summary

Coins are for spending. The Apothecary keeps a counter across the town and sells what mends an Oathbound between fights, and the Innkeeper will not watch another one leave her door with an empty satchel.

### offer_line

Innkeeper: Before you go back up to him. Your satchel is empty; I checked it while you slept, and no, I am not sorry. Take those coins across to the Apothecary and buy a Herb Salve off her, one at least. A salve is a mend you can use when nothing in your party knows how, and up on that road there is no fire and no bed, only what you carried out of my door.

### accept_option

I'll stock up.

### refuse_option

I'll keep my coins.

### accepted_line

Innkeeper: Her counter is over on the west side, by the stalls. Talk to her, look at what is on the shelf, and buy the salve. Twenty coins, and it has bought better people than you another hour.

### refused_line

Innkeeper: Keep your coins, then. They are no use to anybody in a dead Oathkeeper's purse.

### reoffer_line

Innkeeper: Ready to spend a little of that purse?

### progress_line

Innkeeper: The Apothecary. West side of the town, by the stalls. One salve.

### continue_option

On my way.

### abandon_option

Not now.

### abandoned_line

Innkeeper: Your satchel, your funeral.

### complete_line

Apothecary: Good. Now it is in your satchel, use it; a salve in the bag has never healed anybody. Take this vial too, on the house, and tell that Scout of yours I said you were sensible. He has the road waiting for you, and you are as ready for it as I can make you.

### done_line

Apothecary: Salve on the wound, not on the bread. You would be surprised.

---

## The Road Is Waiting

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_01j_the_road_is_waiting.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_01j_the_road_is_waiting.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** apothecary · **Turn-in:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01i_a_stocked_satchel`

### title

The Road Is Waiting

### summary

Bed slept in, satchel stocked, and nothing left in the town that can teach anything. The Apothecary sends the player back up the road to the Scout's fire, where the rite starts in earnest.

### offer_line

Apothecary: Now then. You have slept, you have eaten, and you are carrying something for the first wound. That is everything this town has for you, and I have watched enough champions go out that gate to know the rest of it is not bought over a counter. Go on. Back up the road, to that Scout of yours by the fire, and tell him you are ready.

### accept_option

I'm ready.

### refuse_option

A moment yet.

### accepted_line

Apothecary: Straight out the north gate and up the road. He is sitting at his fire exactly where you left him; he always is.

### refused_line

Apothecary: Take your moment. The seal will not, but take it.

### reoffer_line

Apothecary: Ready to go up to him now?

### progress_line

Apothecary: Out the north gate and up the road. He is at his fire.

### continue_option

On my way.

### abandon_option

Not yet.

### abandoned_line

Apothecary: When you are ready, then.

### complete_line

Scout: There you are, and look at you: fed, rested, and carrying something for the first wound. That is the whole of what I can hand you at a fire. The rest of it is up that road, and the road is where it starts in earnest.

### done_line

Scout: You came back up. Good. Now the rite.

---

## The Ruined Road

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02_the_ruined_road.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02_the_ruined_road.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** scout

**Follows:** `quest_main_01j_the_road_is_waiting`

**Recommended level:** 8 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Ruined Road

### summary

Three offerings go on the altar, and all three have to be carried up the ruined road by hand. Emberlings have taken to that road by the ruins and burn anything that walks it.

### offer_line

Scout: Now it starts in earnest. Three offerings go on that altar, and every one of them is carried up the road on foot. At present the road cannot be walked. Emberlings have taken to it by the ruins and they burn whatever passes. Drive three of them off and the way up is ours again.

### accept_option

Consider it done.

### refuse_option

Not right now.

### accepted_line

Scout: They gather up the road toward the ruins. Strike first if you can; they do not wait for you to be ready.

### refused_line

Scout: Then I will sit by my fire a little longer. The seal is not through yet.

### reoffer_line

Scout: The Emberlings are still on the road. Ready to try?

### progress_line

Scout: How goes the road?

### continue_option

Still at it.

### abandon_option

I can't manage it.

### abandoned_line

Scout: No shame in it. They are fierce little things.

### complete_line

Scout: The road is quiet. Now the rite itself. Three offerings, and every one has to come out of the living world, because that is the one thing the dead king has none of. Water first. The Ranger keeps watch on the far side of the pond, north-east of this camp. Walk up the meadow with the water on your right and you'll find her on the north shore. She draws the stillwater for the altar, and just now she cannot draw a drop of it. Help her.

### done_line

Scout: The Ranger is north-east of here, on the north shore of the pond. Keep the water on your right as you go up and you can't miss her.

### caution_line

Scout: One thing. Those Emberlings are older and meaner than the one the Elder put in your hands. Get your partner closer to level %d before you go looking for trouble; the meadow Loambucks are good practice.

---

## Word with the Ranger

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02_to_the_ranger.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02_to_the_ranger.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** scout · **Turn-in:** ranger

**Follows:** `quest_main_02_the_ruined_road`

### title

Word with the Ranger

### summary

The first of the three offerings is water, and the Ranger draws it. She keeps watch on the north shore of the pond, north-east of the Scout's camp, and something in the shallows has stopped her drawing a drop.

### offer_line

Scout: Go on, then, while the road is quiet. North-east, up the meadow with the water on your right, and you will come out on the north shore. The Ranger is the one standing in it. Tell her I sent you and do whatever she asks, because without her there is no water, and without water there is no rite.

### accept_option

I'll find her.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

Scout: Water on your right the whole way up. You cannot miss her; she does not sit down.

### refused_line

Scout: The pond will still be there. So will she, knee deep and swearing.

### reoffer_line

Scout: Ready to go and see the Ranger?

### progress_line

Scout: North-east, up the meadow. Keep the water on your right.

### complete_line

Ranger: You're the one the scout sent down for the water. Good. Stand there a moment and look at my shallows before you say anything cheerful.

### done_line

Ranger: The Scout's runner. Mind your feet on the stones.

---

## Scalded Shallows

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02a_scalded_shallows.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02a_scalded_shallows.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** ranger

**Follows:** `quest_main_02_to_the_ranger`

**Recommended level:** 9 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

Scalded Shallows

### summary

The altar's first offering is stillwater, drawn cold from the pond. Slaglings out of the pit east of the shallows have it boiling, and the Ranger cannot draw a drop until they are driven back.

### offer_line

Ranger: You're the one the scout sent down for the water? Then you have come at a poor time. Stillwater has to be drawn cold. Boiled water is no offering, it is only water. And Slaglings are crawling out of the pit east of here and sitting in the shallows until the whole shore steams. Drive three of them back and the pit settles.

### accept_option

I'll drive them back.

### refuse_option

Not yet.

### accepted_line

Ranger: They're slow and they're tough. Water and earth put them out quicker than fire does. Your Loambuck will earn its keep here.

### refused_line

Ranger: Then the altar waits, and I keep watching the water boil.

### reoffer_line

Ranger: The shallows are still steaming. Changed your mind?

### progress_line

Ranger: How goes it at the pit?

### continue_option

Still at it.

### abandon_option

I can't manage it.

### abandoned_line

Ranger: They're stubborn things. Come back when you're ready.

### complete_line

Ranger: The water's cooling already. Give it till morning and I'll have your stillwater drawn and stoppered. That is one offering of three. Wood is next, and it has to be cut green and never burned, which is exactly the trouble: the woodcutter in the west wood has been shouting about bats for days and cannot put an axe to anything while they are lighting his stacks.

### done_line

Ranger: The stillwater is drawn. Try the west wood; the woodcutter is waiting on you.

### caution_line

Ranger: Hm. Slaglings hit harder than Emberlings, and yours still look green. I'd want them nearer level %d before wading in. Your call.

---

## Word in the West Wood

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02a_to_the_woodcutter.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02a_to_the_woodcutter.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** ranger · **Turn-in:** woodcutter

**Follows:** `quest_main_02a_scalded_shallows`

### title

Word in the West Wood

### summary

Water is drawn and wood is next, cut green and never burned. The Woodcutter works the west wood, and he has not put an axe to anything for a week.

### offer_line

Ranger: So go and see him. West of here, past the meadow and into the trees; you will hear him before you see him, because he has been shouting about bats since Tuesday. Tell him the water is drawn. It may cheer him up, though I doubt it.

### accept_option

West it is.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

Ranger: Straight west. Follow the sound of a man arguing with the sky.

### refused_line

Ranger: The wood is not going anywhere, and neither are his bats.

### reoffer_line

Ranger: Ready to go west and see the Woodcutter?

### progress_line

Ranger: West, into the trees. Listen for the shouting.

### complete_line

Woodcutter: Ranger sent you? Bless her. Then you are here about the heartwood, and I am here about the bats, and you are going to hear about the bats first.

### done_line

Woodcutter: Mind the stacks. They go up quicker than you would think.

---

## Word with the Warden

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02b_to_the_warden.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02b_to_the_warden.tres</sub>

Side quest · **Giver:** woodcutter · **Turn-in:** warden

**Follows:** `quest_main_02b_wings_in_the_wood`

### title

Word with the Warden

### summary

The last offering comes out of the Order's own graves, and only a warden may ask for it. Serah is camped at the edge of the ruins, north-east, and she came down the road the night the bells rang.

### offer_line

Woodcutter: The last one is not mine to give, so go and stand in front of somebody it is. North-east, up where the road climbs into the ruins. Serah is camped at the edge of them. She is a warden of the Order, she is not warm, and she will be worth every cold word of it.

### accept_option

I'll go up.

### refuse_option

Give me a moment.

### accepted_line

Woodcutter: Follow the road up past the pond and keep climbing. You will see her fire before you see her.

### refused_line

Woodcutter: Take your time. She has waited on the Order before.

### reoffer_line

Woodcutter: Ready to go up and see the Warden?

### progress_line

Woodcutter: North-east, up the road, at the edge of the ruins.

### complete_line

Warden: Stand still. Water and wood, and now you come up here for the third, which means somebody has finally told you where the iron comes from. Sit down. This part is ours, and it is not pleasant.

### done_line

Warden: Rest a moment. I'll see your Oathbound mended.

---

## Wings in the Wood

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02b_wings_in_the_wood.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02b_wings_in_the_wood.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** woodcutter

**Follows:** `quest_main_02a_to_the_woodcutter`

**Recommended level:** 11 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

Wings in the Wood

### summary

The altar's second offering is heartwood, cut green and never burned. Scorchbats have roosted in the west wood and lit the woodcutter's stacks twice, and nothing can be cut while they hunt.

### offer_line

Woodcutter: Ranger sent you? Bless her. You'll be after the heartwood for the altar, and I'd have had it cut a week ago if it weren't for the bats. Scorchbats, roosted in my wood, and twice now they've had my stacks alight. Burnt wood is no good to anybody up there. Clear three out and you'll have your brand by nightfall.

### accept_option

I'll clear them out.

### refuse_option

Maybe later.

### accepted_line

Woodcutter: They swoop on anyone who gets close. Strike first if you can, and keep your Loambuck ready to patch up whoever takes the burns.

### refused_line

Woodcutter: I'll be here, beating out fires.

### reoffer_line

Woodcutter: Still bats in my wood. You up for it now?

### progress_line

Woodcutter: Any luck with the roost?

### continue_option

Working on it.

### abandon_option

They're too fast for me.

### abandoned_line

Woodcutter: Can't blame you. Come back when you've got your feet under you.

### complete_line

Woodcutter: Quiet! First quiet night in a week. I'll cut your heartwood at first light, green and clean, the way it has to go up. That is two of the three. The last one is not mine to give; it comes out of our own graves, and only a warden may ask for it. Serah is camped at the edge of the ruins, north-east. She came down the road the night the bells rang.

### done_line

Woodcutter: The warden is at the edge of the ruins, north-east. Tell her I sent you, and tell her the wood is cut.

### caution_line

Woodcutter: Mind, these bats are no meadow pests. I've seen them tear through Oathbound tougher-looking than yours. Nearer level %d, I'd say, before you go poking at the roost.

---

## The Hollow Watch

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_02c_the_hollow_watch.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_02c_the_hollow_watch.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** warden

**Follows:** `quest_main_02b_to_the_warden`

**Recommended level:** 13 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Hollow Watch

### summary

The altar's last offering is seal-iron, the sigil the Order buries with its own. The graves west of the altar are stirring, and a Cinderclaw holds the last stretch of road, so the Warden will not let anyone lift a sigil until both are dealt with.

### offer_line

Warden: So you're the one the woodcutter keeps talking about. I'm Serah, warden of the Order. Water and wood you have. The third offering is ours: seal-iron, the sigil every one of us is buried with, and it must be lifted from the graves by hand. The trouble is that the graves are stirring, as they always stir when the seal thins, and there is a Cinderclaw squatting on the last stretch of road besides. Put two of the squires back to rest, and the Cinderclaw down with them.

### accept_option

I'll face them.

### refuse_option

I need more time.

### accepted_line

Warden: The graves are just west of the altar. The Cinderclaw stalks the road where the paving starts. Come back to me between fights; I'll see your Oathbound mended.

### refused_line

Warden: Take your time. The graves have waited a hundred years; they'll wait a few more days.

### reoffer_line

Warden: Ready to face the graves?

### progress_line

Warden: The graves still stir. How do you fare?

### continue_option

I'm going back.

### abandon_option

It's beyond me.

### abandoned_line

Warden: No shame in knowing your limits. Grow, and return.

### complete_line

Warden: Two squires at rest, the Cinderclaw down, and the seal-iron in my hand. Water, wood and iron. The rite is whole. Sit down, then, because there is one thing left standing between you and that altar, and you have known his name since you could talk.

### done_line

Warden: The graves are quiet and the rite is gathered. Only the knight is left.

### caution_line

Warden: I won't stop you. Understand what you are facing, though. Those squires walked this road as champions before you did, and they remember how to fight. If your lead were nearer level %d, I'd sleep easier.

---

## The Oathbreaker

<!-- key: quest:quest_main_03_the_black_knight.tres -->

<sub>game/content/quests/quest_main_03_the_black_knight.tres</sub>

Main quest · **Giver:** warden

**Follows:** `quest_main_02c_the_hollow_watch`

**Recommended level:** 15 (`%d` in the caution line)

### title

The Oathbreaker

### summary

The rite is gathered, and the Oathbreaker keeps the altar as he has kept it for every champion before. He is not an enemy, but he does not stand aside for anyone who cannot put him down, because whatever waits under the altar is worse.

### offer_line

Warden: The knight at the altar was one of the dead king's own, once. When the king reached past what a king may touch, the magic went through his knights before it ever reached his son, and it took the man's oath out of him whether he willed it or not. That is the name he carries. He turned all the same, and he has stood in front of that altar ever since, on our side of it. He is not your enemy. He is your last gate. Nobody goes down to the king who cannot first beat the Oathbreaker, because the king is worse. Bring him down and he will stand aside himself. Will you face him?

### accept_option

I will face the knight.

### refuse_option

I need to prepare first.

### accepted_line

Warden: Let me mend your Oathbound first. Then take him the way you would take the king: everything you have, all at once. Keep your Loambuck ready, because this fight will be long. He will not kill you. He never has. That is not what he is for.

### refused_line

Warden: Wise. Come back when you are ready. He is not going anywhere; that is rather the point of him.

### reoffer_line

Warden: The Oathbreaker still keeps the altar. Are you ready now?

### progress_line

Warden: The knight still stands. Rest here before you go up.

### continue_option

I'm going back up.

### abandon_option

I can't beat it.

### abandoned_line

Warden: Then we wait and grow stronger. He is patient, and so can we be.

### complete_line

Warden: He stood aside for you? Then it is done, and it has begun. I saw the light come up over the ruins from here. Go down while it burns, put the king back under, and come home. In thirty years you will be the one sitting at the edge of these ruins, telling some frightened child that the knight will not kill them.

### done_line

Warden: The passage is open and the light is holding. Whatever is down there, it has never yet been more than we could carry.

### caution_line

Warden: One more thing. He goes easy on nobody, and he is stronger than anything you have faced. I would not send a champion whose lead is below level %d. Train on the graves and in the wood if you must; he has waited a great deal longer than that.

---
